components.title: Practical Test or Alternative to Practical
components.format: Laboratory experiment skills or written alternative assessing practical and investigative skills

objectives.wording: Describe how to measure a variety of lengths with appropriate precision using tapes, rulers and micrometers (including reading the scale on an analogue micrometer)
Describe how to use a measuring cylinder to measure the volume of a liquid and to determine the volume of a solid by displacement
Describe how to measure a variety of time intervals using clocks and digital timers
Determine an average value for a small distance and for a short interval of time by measuring multiples (including the period of oscillation of a pendulum)
Understand that a scalar quantity has magnitude (size) only and that a vector quantity has magnitude and direction
Know that the following quantities are scalars: distance, speed, time, mass, energy and temperature
Know that the following quantities are vectors: displacement, force, weight, velocity, acceleration, momentum, electric field strength and gravitational field strength
Determine, by calculation or graphically, the resultant of two vectors at right angles
Define speed as distance travelled per unit time; recall and use the equation v = s / t
Define velocity as speed in a given direction
Define acceleration as change in velocity per unit time; recall and use the equation a = Δv / Δt = (v - u) / t
Sketch, plot and interpret distance–time and speed–time graphs
Determine from the shape of a speed–time graph when an object is: (a) at rest, (b) moving with constant speed, (c) moving with constant acceleration, (d) moving with changing acceleration
State that acceleration of free fall g for an object close to the surface of the Earth is approximately constant and is approximately 9.8 m/s²
State that mass is a measure of the quantity of matter in an object at rest relative to the observer
State that weight is a gravitational force on an object that has mass; recall and use W = mg
Describe and use the concept of gravitational field strength g as force per unit mass; g = W / m
Define density as mass per unit volume; recall and use the equation ρ = m / V
Describe experiments to determine the density of a liquid, of a regularly shaped solid and of an irregularly shaped solid which sinks in a liquid
Identify forces acting on an object and determine the resultant force
Recall and use the equation F = ma and know that the force and acceleration are in the same direction
Describe Hooke’s law and recall and use the equation F = kΔx
Define the moment of a force as moment = force × perpendicular distance from the pivot
Apply the principle of moments to balance problems involving clockwise and anticlockwise moments
Define momentum as mass × velocity; recall and use p = mv
Apply the principle of conservation of momentum to solve simple problems in one dimension
Define impulse as force × time; recall and use impulse = FΔt = Δ(mv)
Recall and use the equation for kinetic energy Ek = 1/2 m v²
Recall and use the equation for gravitational potential energy ΔEp = mgΔh
State and apply the principle of the conservation of energy to energy transformations
Recall and use the equation for work done W = Fd = ΔE
Define power as work done per unit time or energy transferred per unit time; recall and use P = W / t = ΔE / t
Recall and use efficiency = (useful energy output / total energy input) × 100%
Define pressure as force per unit area; recall and use p = F / A
Recall and use the equation for hydrostatic pressure in a liquid Δp = ρgΔh
Describe the states of matter and their interconversion in terms of the kinetic particle model
Explain the relationship between temperature and the kinetic energy of particles, including the Kelvin scale where T(K) = θ(°C) + 273
Explain the pressure of a gas in terms of particle collisions with container walls; recall and use p1V1 = p2V2 for constant temperature
Describe thermal expansion of solids, liquids and gases and explain its consequences and applications
Define specific heat capacity c as thermal energy required to raise the temperature of 1 kg by 1 °C; recall and use c = ΔE / (mΔθ)
Describe melting, boiling, solidification and condensation in terms of latent heat and particle behavior without change in temperature
Describe thermal conduction in terms of atomic vibrations and free/delocalised electrons in metals
Describe convection in fluids in terms of density changes and convection currents
Describe thermal radiation as electromagnetic waves (infrared) and the factors affecting emission and absorption
Know that waves transfer energy without transferring matter
Describe transverse and longitudinal waves and give examples of each
Define speed, frequency, wavelength and amplitude; recall and use the wave equation v = f λ
Describe the reflection of light at a plane surface; law of reflection: angle of incidence = angle of reflection
Describe refraction of light and define refractive index n; recall and use n = sin(i) / sin(r) and n = c / v
Describe total internal reflection and critical angle c; recall and use n = 1 / sin(c)
Describe the action of a thin converging lens on a parallel beam of light; define focal length and principal focus
Know the main regions of the electromagnetic spectrum in order of frequency and wavelength: radio, microwave, infrared, visible, ultraviolet, X-ray, gamma
Know that all electromagnetic waves travel at the speed of light in vacuum (3.0 × 10⁸ m/s)
Describe the production of sound waves by vibrating sources and transmission as longitudinal waves
State that the approximate range of audible frequencies for a healthy human ear is 20 Hz to 20 000 Hz
Describe the forces between magnetic poles and between magnets and magnetic materials (attraction and repulsion)
Describe a magnetic field as a region in which a magnetic pole experiences a force; plot magnetic field lines with a compass
State that there are positive and negative charges measured in coulombs; unlike charges attract and like charges repel
Define electric current as the charge passing a point per unit time; recall and use the equation I = Q / t
Describe electrical conduction in metals in terms of the movement of free electrons
State that conventional current is from positive to negative and that the flow of free electrons is from negative to positive
Describe the use of ammeters (analogue and digital) with different ranges
Define e.m.f. (electromotive force) as electrical work done by a source in moving a unit charge around a complete circuit; recall and use E = W / Q
Define p.d. (potential difference) as work done by a unit charge passing through a component; recall and use V = W / Q
Describe the use of voltmeters (analogue and digital) with different ranges
Recall and use the equation resistance = p.d. / current, R = V / I
Describe an experiment to determine resistance using a voltmeter and an ammeter and do the appropriate calculations
Recall and use, for a wire, the direct proportionality between resistance and length, and inverse proportionality between resistance and cross-sectional area
State Ohm’s law, including reference to constant temperature
Sketch and explain the current–voltage graphs for a resistor of constant resistance, a filament lamp and a diode
Describe the effect of temperature increase on the resistance of a resistor, such as the filament in a filament lamp

Draw and interpret circuit diagrams with cells, batteries, power supplies, generators, oscilloscopes, potential dividers, switches, resistors (fixed and variable), heaters, thermistors (NTC only), light-dependent resistors (LDRs), lamps, motors, ammeters, voltmeters, magnetising coils, transformers, fuses, relays, diodes and light-emitting diodes (LEDs), and know how these components behave in the circuit

Recall and use in calculations, the fact that: (a) current at every point in a series circuit is the same, (b) sum of currents entering a junction equals sum leaving, (c) total p.d. across components in series equals sum of individual p.d.s, (d) p.d. across parallel branches is the same
Calculate the combined resistance of two or more resistors in series; R = R1 + R2 + ...
Calculate the combined resistance of two resistors in parallel; 1/R = 1/R1 + 1/R2
Calculate current, voltage and resistance in parts of a circuit or in the whole circuit

objectives.section: 4.3.3 Action and use of circuit components
objectives.wording: Describe the action of a variable potential divider

objectives.section: 4.3.3 Action and use of circuit components
objectives.wording: Recall and use the equation for two resistors used as a potential divider: R1 / R2 = V1 / V2
Recall and use the equation power = current × voltage, P = I V
Recall and use the equation energy = current × voltage × time, E = I V t
State the hazards of damaged insulation, overheating cables, damp conditions, and excess current from overloading
Explain the use and operation of trip switches and fuses and choose appropriate fuse ratings and trip switch settings
Describe an experiment to demonstrate electromagnetic induction
Know that a current-carrying coil in a magnetic field may experience a turning effect, increased by turns, current, and field strength
Recall and use the equation Vp / Vs = Np / Ns where P and S refer to primary and secondary

subtopics.title: The nuclear model of the atom

objectives.wording: Describe the structure of the atom in terms of a positively charged nucleus and negatively charged electrons in orbit around the nucleus
Describe the composition of the nucleus in terms of protons and neutrons
Define proton number (atomic number) Z and nucleon number (mass number) A and calculate the number of neutrons
Explain what is meant by an isotope and state that an element may have more than one isotope
Describe the characteristics of the three types of emission (alpha, beta, gamma) in terms of ionising power and penetrating power
Define half-life as the time taken for half the nuclei of that isotope in any sample to decay; calculate half-life from decay curves
Know that the Earth is a planet that orbits the Sun once in approximately 365 days and that it rotates on its axis once in approximately 24 hours
Describe the Solar System as containing: the Sun, eight planets (Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune), dwarf planets, moons, asteroids and comets
Analyse and interpret planetary data about orbital distance, orbital duration, density, surface temperature and gravitational field strength
Recall and use the equation for orbital speed v = 2 π r / T
State that the Sun is a star of medium size consisting mostly of hydrogen and helium, radiating energy from nuclear fusion

Describe the life cycle of stars: interstellar clouds (nebulae), protostar, stable star (main sequence), red giant or red supergiant, planetary nebula or supernova, white dwarf, neutron star or black hole
State that the Milky Way is one of billions of galaxies; define light-year as the distance travelled in a vacuum by light in one year (approximately 9.5 × 10¹⁵ m)
Describe redshift in the light from distant galaxies and how redshift provides evidence that the Universe is expanding (Big Bang Theory)
